title: The worm box runs dry
about: A warm dry spell dries the worm box's bedding. The mist line under its lid waters it from the rain barrel, with the box closed: the edge proposes it, you confirm. In frost it waits.

steps.title: The bedding dries out
steps.why: Worms breathe through their skin: below about half its moisture the bedding is too dry, and they slow down. The moisture probe in the box tells the keeper.

expect.say: the keeper sees a dry box: {v}

steps.title: Mist the box from the rain barrel
steps.why: The mist line is a drip hose under the lid, fed from the barrel through a valve the edge opens. Rainwater, no chlorine, and the box stays closed. It runs half a litre a minute and stops when the dose is given.

steps.title: A cold snap
steps.why: The air falls far below freezing. The keeper holds feeding and watering, the worm box's too: water on frozen bedding freezes the worms.

steps.title: In frost the dry box waits
steps.why: The box dries again, but nothing is proposed while it is freezing: the keeper says the box is dry, and the mist line waits for warmer air.

do.label: Let the box dry out again

expect.say: the keeper sees a dry box: {v}

steps.title: Calm again
steps.why: The cold passes. Once the air and the box are clearly warmer, the keeper lets go of the hold and the mist line is proposed again.
